5.label: Command or request
5.text: The same demand delivered as a command and as a request produces materially different results from the same people. Tone, humility and the manner of the ask often decide the outcome. Use this with Setting and Establishing.

5.label: Understanding the why
5.text: Knowledge hoarding produces compliance without capability: people follow procedures they do not understand, for reasons they were never told. Audit one process your team follows without being able to explain why, then explain it or change it.

6.label: Clarity
6.text: Many operational failures happen because people in authority believe execution needs their presence when it needs their clarity. Authority travels with a clear instruction.

6.label: Capability
6.text: Strategy is weakened when leaders become so committed to movement that they ignore capability gaps. A disciplined readiness pause can prevent an expensive failure later.

6.label: Commitment
6.text: Commitments lose strategic meaning when they are honoured only when convenient. Good intent has limited value if people cannot understand what is required of them.

7.label: Networked execution
7.text: Outcomes depend on a web of contributors beyond the visible leaders. Map and value the wider contribution system.

7.label: External
7.text: Many partnerships fail because the terms were vague at the start and each party assumed the other had agreed to something slightly different. Before formalising, write down what each party contributes, what each expects in return and how long the arrangement runs.

8.label: Granted and accepted
8.text: A mandate can be signed off in a board paper and carry no weight on the ground until the people who must act on it accept it. Ask who has not yet accepted the expectation, and spend your effort winning that acceptance.

10.label: Concession under pressure
10.text: A commitment that reverses as soon as the pressure lifts was a concession all along. Build commitments that hold without the pressure.

10.label: Agreement on the surface
10.text: Teams often say yes to a new way of working while quietly keeping the old habits underneath. People who keep both systems running have committed to neither. Bring the hidden habits into the open.

11.label: 4 · Strengthening Accountability
11.text: The gap between stated intention and actual behaviour is one of the most revealing leadership diagnostics. Build accountability into the space between the commitment and the moment of execution. Its purpose is to close the gap between what people sincerely intend and what they do when pressure arrives.

12.label: Engagement becomes transactional
12.text: Many teams run on minimum compliance: do what is required, claim the credit, defend the boundary. Covenantal teams notice when a colleague is overwhelmed and carry the extra load, and they follow up after the project ends. Ask: is our team culture contractual or covenantal?

12.label: Quiet non-participation
12.text: Indifference is the most underestimated risk to a strategic agenda, because quiet non-participation is invisible. Identify the people who have neither opposed nor engaged the initiative, ask each one directly whether they are in, and bring them in or redesign around them.

16.label: 1 · Start With the Future
16.text: Leaders who brief tasks before establishing the why, the who and the what-for produce people who execute without conviction. Establish the purpose first.

16.label: Explaining the mandate
16.text: Leaders must be able to explain why the work is legitimate, who authorised it and how it connects to the larger mission, alongside what their teams are doing.

17.label: Evaluate
17.text: Leaders should be able to hear raw frustration without immediately defending the system or correcting the emotion. Credibility grows when leaders acknowledge the gap between intention and execution and work to close it.

17.label: Listening discipline
17.text: Speaking before understanding is a common leadership failure. People perform better when difficulty does not automatically threaten their belonging or worth.

18.label: Questions open
18.text: Responding with a question returns ownership of the response to the person and gives them space to examine their own position without defending against an external judgement. Questions open where corrections close.
